featured_videos.title: What to Buy at the Store | Getting Started
featured_videos.creator: Butter Bob Briggs
featured_videos.editorial_title: What to Buy at the Store | Getting Started
featured_videos.commentary: Butter Bob's back, and honestly, the community's reaction tells you everything you need to know about what's missing from this space right now. People aren't just grateful for a grocery store walkthrough, they're grateful for someone who shows up, stays calm, and doesn't overcomplicate things. That "nothing with anything" line is gold because it cuts through all the noise, and the comments show people are starving for straightforward, no-agenda guidance when they're starting out. If you're new and feeling overwhelmed by all the macro debates and supplement rabbit holes, this is the kind of real-world help that actually works, grab our food list to take with you, and keep it that simple.

featured_videos.title: The Carnivore Diet + Walking...Here's What Happened
featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Quest
featured_videos.editorial_title: The Carnivore Diet + Walking.Here's What Happened
featured_videos.commentary: The comment that stuck with me here is the one about progress over perfection, because it's exactly right. Larry walked 21 days in October. He missed five, ate some soup that wasn't textbook carnivore when he was sick, and the internet's first instinct was to tell him it doesn't work. But here's what actually matters: he's still showing up. He didn't use illness or imperfection as a reason to quit, and that's the version of this way of eating that lasts. From my experience coaching, I've seen people get further on 80% consistency they can maintain than on 100% perfection they abandon in week three. The other thing jumping out at me is how many people in the comments are reporting real wins. down 7 pounds in a week, 16 pounds in a month after a stall, Halloween with zero candy. and they're crediting the same thing Larry is: just staying in the game. That's the unglamorous truth nobody wants to film.

featured_videos.title: The BBC Went After Carnivore. I Was In It.
featured_videos.creator: Shawn Baker MD
featured_videos.editorial_title: The BBC Went After Carnivore. I Was In It.
featured_videos.commentary: The comments here are pretty telling. people aren't mad about the science anymore, they're just tired of being told what to eat by institutions they don't trust. That's actually the bigger story than the BBC segment itself. What's interesting is watching the community spot the fiber argument (that bit about pooping more equals better health) and just. not buy it. That's a shift from two years ago when people were still defensive about digestion. Now they're calling it what it is: confusing output with outcome. The real win isn't proving carnivore right on camera. It's that fewer people need permission from mainstream media to trust what they're experiencing themselves.

featured_videos.title: I Tried World’s Most Controversial Diet For 72 Hours
featured_videos.creator: TacoTina11
featured_videos.editorial_title: I Tried World’s Most Controversial Diet For 72 Hours
featured_videos.commentary: The engineering student comment nails it, and so does the 66-year-old who said it took three weeks to hit his stride. Seventy-two hours on carnivore is basically the adaptation period where your body's still figuring out what's happening, not the payoff period where you actually feel the difference. Most people I've coached need at least two weeks before they stop thinking about food every afternoon, and closer to a month before the energy piece clicks into place. The real test isn't how you feel on day three. it's whether you can stick with it long enough to know if it works for *your* body, not just for the algorithm.

featured_videos.title: This Carnivore Casserole Is All I Want to Eat
featured_videos.creator: Meet Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: This Carnivore Casserole Is All I Want to Eat
featured_videos.commentary: The casserole thing is genius because it solves the hardest problem most people face: what to actually cook that isn't just meat on a plate. Pork rind crust is the kind of detail that makes someone go "oh, I can do *this*" instead of defaulting to ground beef for the hundredth time. The comments are full of people who've already bought the book and made the recipe, which tells you the video isn't just entertaining, it's actually moving people to cook. That's the gap a lot of carnivore content misses. you can talk macros and protocols all day, but showing someone how to make something delicious they want to eat again next week? That's what sticks.

featured_videos.title: Zrobisz w 3 minuty! Codzienne ciasto jogurtowe / sernik - keto, carnivore
featured_videos.creator: kierunek zdrowie
featured_videos.editorial_title: Zrobisz w 3 minuty! Codzienne ciasto jogurtowe / sernik - keto, carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: Here's the thing about yogurt-based carnivore desserts. they're a gateway to actually sticking with this way of eating long-term, and the comments show that people are getting creative with what they have on hand. Someone mentioned making it with skyr instead of yogurt and adjusting the sweetness, which is exactly the kind of problem-solving that works better than rigid recipes. The pushback on powdered sweeteners is fair too (one commenter prefers berries and cinnamon baked with eggs and fat), but the point isn't whether you use allulose or not. it's that you're not standing in front of the bakery case at 7 pm hungry and frustrated. Simple wins over perfect, every time.
